Manage and refer urgently:

If temperature ≥ 38°C or meningitis likely: give ceftriaxone1 2g IM. Avoid injecting > 1g IM at one injection site. If referral delayed, repeat ceftriaxone1 2g IM after 12 hours. Give single dose paracetamol 1g and/or ibuprofen2 400mg for pain. If pain severe, also give single dose tramadol 50mg.
If fever now or in past 3 days, and in a malaria area in past 3 months, malaria likely 39.
HEADACHE

1If severe penicillin allergy (previous angioedema, anaphylaxis or urticaria), discuss with doctor. 2Avoid ibuprofen if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant. 3History of anaphylaxis, urticaria or angioedema.

Yes Migraine likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) or ibuprofen2 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days. • If nausea, also give metoclopramide 10mg 8 hourly up to 3 doses. • Advise to recognise and treat migraine early, rest in dark, quiet room. • Advise regular meals, keep hydrated, regular exercise, good sleep hygiene. • Keep a headache diary to identify triggers: lack of sleep, hunger, stress, caffeine, chocolate, cheese. Avoid if possible. • Avoid oestrogen-containing contraceptives 170. • If ≥ 2 attacks/month, refer/discuss for medication to prevent migraines.
No • Check BP. If ≥ 140/90 148. • Ask about type and site of pain:
Advise to use analgesia only when necessary. Overuse may cause headaches: if using analgesia > 2 days/week
for ≥ 3 months, advise to reduce amount used. Headache should improve within 2 months of decreased use.
Patient > 50 years, pain over temples Tightness around head or generalised

Yes Sinusitis likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) for up to 5 days. • Give sodium chloride 0.9% nose drops as needed. • Give oxymetazoline 0.05% 2 drops in each nostril 8 hourly for up to 5 days. Advise against overuse which may worsen blocked nose. • If symptoms ≥ 10 days, fever ≥ 38°C, purulent nasal discharge, facial pain ≥ 3 days, or symptoms worsen after initial improvement, give amoxicillin 500mg 8 hourly for 5 days. If severe penicillin allergy3, give instead azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days. • If recurrent, test for HIV 124. • If tooth infection or swelling over sinus/around eye, refer same day.
No • If patient has been in a malaria area in past 3 months, malaria likely 39. • If patient has a tick bite (small dark brown/ black scab) or tick present, tick bite fever likely 38.

- Advise on cough/sneeze hygiene and to
wash hands regularly. While unwell, avoid contact with elderly/those with long-term health conditions. - Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly
